The commit message carries purpose and verification with the brief guaranteed identical to the removed text, in the shortest form and with no Markdown label in a commit message. It carries both costs at once: the task-list tool gains an output on success and every fixed completion call a captured print to join, and the boundary between brief and bar rests only on the unchecked prose-versus-bullets convention, with no label keeping the bar from being read as an authoring contract.

open-question.question: Which fields does one line of the milestones tool's `tasks` query carry, in what order and with what separator, given that the draft lists date, milestone path, and task title, that a title may hold spaces, and that a reader wanting a task's diff needs its commit hash or must search subjects itself?
open-question.alternative: Each line carries exactly the draft's three fields, in the draft's order: the commit date as YYYY-MM-DD, the milestone path, and the task title (the `Task-completion:` subject with its marker stripped), separated by single tab characters, the title last. No commit hash is printed; a reader wanting a task's diff searches subjects itself. Matches the draft as written and the plugin's one existing tab-separated listing (the open-question tool's `list --with-question` prints id, tab, question text), so a title holding spaces needs no positional rule and the shape stays the smallest that serves the five readers, none of which opens a task's diff today. A reader that does want the diff has to recover the commit from the title by its own `git log --grep` or subject search, the hand-composed git pipeline the milestones tool exists to end, and a title reused across milestones (follow-up work may reuse a done title) makes that search ambiguous.

Each line carries four fields: the commit's abbreviated hash as git's `%h` prints it, then the date as YYYY-MM-DD, the milestone path, and the task title, separated by single tab characters, the title last. Every line names the exact commit, so a reader reaches the task's diff or full body with one `git show` and never searches subjects, even for a reused title; it leads with the hash as the draft's own `since` query does, and the tab keeps a spaced title unambiguous for both a person and a split on tab. Adds a field none of the five readers this milestone moves onto `tasks` reads, and puts a git term in front of a line the draft means to speak in the workflow's vocabulary (milestone, task) rather than git's; tabs also render as uneven columns in a terminal.

Each line carries four fields: the abbreviated hash as `%h` prints it, the date as YYYY-MM-DD, the milestone path, and the task title, separated by single spaces, the title last and taking the rest of the line, so a parser splits on the first three spaces only (the hash, the date, and a milestone path the milestone-definition tool slugs carry no space). Reads like the `git log --oneline` form and the draft's `since` line (hash, date, subject), with the diff one `git show` away, while a person sees plain text with no tab characters. Unambiguous only while no field before the title can hold a space: the hash and date never do, but a milestone path holding one (a hand-made or moved directory) would split wrongly with no error, so the line's correctness rests on the slug rule rather than on its separator.

Each line carries the draft's three fields with no hash: the date as YYYY-MM-DD, the milestone path, and the task title, separated by single spaces, the title last and taking the rest of the line, so a parser splits on the first two spaces only. The plainest line for the readers that only read it as text (finish's summary bullets, `ask-in-milestone-context`, the two triage skills' already-addressed checks), with no tab characters and no git term, exactly the draft's fields. Carries both costs of its two positions: a reader wanting the diff must search subjects itself, and splitting the title off is safe only while milestone paths stay space-free, which the separator does not guarantee.
